title: Annotatio III §.VIII: XIV–XV reformers — Rupert/Ascelinus consub, or ancient supernatural/spiritual presence kept
pass_a_gloss: Nay from the Reformers of pontifical Idolomania there arose in both the fourteenth and the fifteenth Century those who partly restored Rupert of Deutz and Ascelinus on Consubstantiation, whether Crasser or Subtler, partly the Ancients’ and the pristine Church’s [teaching] on the Supernatural and Spiritual presence of Christ’s Body in the Holy Supper, and keep it even to this day — not delayed by the brute thunderbolt cast out by Trent.
pass_b_english: Fourteenth- and fifteenth-century reformers of pontifical idolomania also rose.

Some restore Rupert of Deutz and Ascelinus on Consubstantiation (crasser or subtler); others restore the pristine Church’s supernatural and spiritual presence of Christ’s body in the Supper — and keep it to this day, undeterred by Trent’s brute thunderbolt.
source_text: Quinimo ex Reformatoribus Pontificiæ Idolomaniæ, tàm XIV. quàm XV. Seculo exsurrexerunt, qui partim Ruperti Tuitiensis & Ascelini, de Consubstantiatione, vel Crassiori, vel Subtiliori, partim Veterum pristinæque Ecclesiæ de Supernaturali & Spirituali Corporis Christi in S. Coena præsentia, reducem fecerunt, inque hodiernum usque diem servant, haud morati fulmen brutum expelvi Tridentina.

lemmas.gloss: of Rupert of Deutz and Ascelinus
